title: Needs you
how: Only what is open for you, oldest first. Each item says what to do, links everything it needs, and gives my recommendation. It leaves this page once you have answered it here or done it.
Pick an answer under each item; a note is optional.
foot: One page, one link, kept current (his order of 2 November). The same list is kept as plain data beside it (items.json) for the advisor's checker.

sections.name: Next week's order (9 to 16 November), drafted by the advisor from your running list, every line your words or your picks. Three changes need your eye: your yes of 6 November becomes standing week to week; the tailor boss's criteria become your rule; the old open items fold into this week's and the archive is dropped, except at most ten that come back to you as one keep-or-drop list. Adopt the order of 9 November?
sections.recommendation: Yes: it holds your rulings and picks of 4 to 8 November and keeps the week at about 83% of its hours. On your tap its rules are recorded, the old items folded in, and its items worked in order beside the old order's last hours, at full speed to Monday 13:00. Nothing in it is acted on before your tap. No web link: the full text is under Read it here.
detail: His order of 9 November 2026

Drafted by the advisor on Sunday 8 November from the running list (https://claude.ai/artifact/Y7jntG2ufSERmAu7TQpcfH), every line his words or his picks; adopted by his tap on his page. Runs from that tap to Monday 16 November, 13:00 Swiss time. Where it and an earlier ruling disagree, this order wins. The ledger works as before (statuses, tools/order_ledger.py); IDs n09-*.
1. Record first, then never restate in an order (RULINGS.md and CLAUDE.md, within their caps)

1. His yes of 6 November stands from week to week: sessions round the clock (nothing touching Unreal during the night's build and walk), up to four helpers, waiting-list items whenever the week's items wait; paced by the weekly line (90% by Monday 07:00, a tenth kept for him, full speed after 07:00).

2. Full scope stays the target (the Hook and the docks, 15 to 20 hours, late 2027); no path chosen on extrapolated numbers; production accelerates as the bottlenecks fall. If cost per piece has not clearly fallen by 1 February, scope moves first, never quality. (5 and 6 Nov)
3. Deep before wide: one dense district proves the method, then the game goes wide. (6 Nov)
4. People in motion are won by research, creativity and trial and error; no money for motion capture. (6 Nov)

5. Testing leans on AI so that what reaches his hands is 99% done; lean: the smallest checks that catch real faults, one added only when a fault slipped past, dropped after a month of catching nothing. (6 and 7 Nov)
6. Records and process stay under about 15% of spend, measured every Monday; the rules are pruned once a month. (6 Nov)
7. From phase 3, short rough feel checks for him, judged only on whether it is fun, apart from the polished plays. (6 Nov)

8. Research before the first try, scaled to the item (a skill or the playbook counts), noted in a few lines. After two failed tries a fault is set aside and listed; one genuinely different method found by research is allowed (about 2 hours); further tries, up to four in all, only while each closes the gap to the bar by at least a third and adds no new fault. None of this asks him. (7 Nov)

9. Models (the replay of 8 Nov): Opus for the session, code, diagnosis, engine research and final reviews; Sonnet for extraction, first readings, routine imports and first small reviews. A fix to a tool that reads real files is checked on those files before it counts. Re-test when a new model arrives.

10. Clothing is not solved by an interim pass. The tailor boss falls only when a garment set passes the 2026 bar close up (photographs, a fresh reviewer, his eye), holds in walk, sit and turn on film, the cast wear distinct outfits, and repeats are cheap (pattern library, skill, the latest of a kind at about half the first). No second Marvelous month unless he decides about 20 November; quality wins over the date. (6 to 8 Nov)
11. Parked 1990 cars, fictional makes, come with phase 2. (6 Nov)
12. Standing habits: smaller pictures for first-round reviews, full size only for final reviews and his page; startup files edited at most once a day. (6 Nov)
2. The week: about 99 of about 120 main-line hours (83%); helpers count against their item

- `n09-1` Phase 1's exit, Monday: one fresh reviewer per exit on the newest build, no bar reworded; his rulings on each open fault on his page, with the advisor's recommendation (looks into phase 2; card memory and headroom first in phase 2); the phase-1 playbook distilled per discipline as the exit's last step. Done: his rulings recorded. 8 h, 7%.
- `n09-2` Tom as one whole person on his page by Tuesday: walk film, sit, talk close-up, outfit. Done: his look answered. 3 h, 2%.

- `n09-3` Card memory and frame headroom, phase 2's first item, from MEMORY-PLAN-2026-11-07: the peak frame at High, game alone, against the budget Windows gives; triangle budgets for the shop displays and Mickey's fittings. Done: peak and steady use under budget in a packaged walk, or the measured gap and its next step. 14 h, 12%.

- `n09-4` Phase 2's plan: Quay Street's pieces, each with an estimate, measured weekly on the progress page beside the 2027 line, the efficiency scoreboard and the PS5 gap list. Done: on the progress page. 5 h, 4%.

- `n09-5` One complete named person, end to end, on Ron: body, face, clothes, voice, routine, talk and the gate, every hour and dollar logged. Done: Ron on his page as a whole person with his cost table. 16 h, 13%.

- `n09-6` Clothing: Sheila out of the white base layer by the refit route; the close-up fixes (jeans stitching, boot laces, hem rib); Epic's resizing clothing on Tom's garments by Wednesday; first pattern-library entries; the garment skill updated; hours per garment on the scoreboard; if room, the first 1990 working jacket in Marvelous. Done: Sheila at the floor; the resizing verdict with numbers. 18 h, 15%.
- `n09-7` Hair decided: cards against strands at Tom's camera and in talk, frame cost, the colour hand-over, Tom's crown; one recommendation. Done: on his page. 6 h, 5%.

- `n09-8` People alive, first steps from ALIVE-PROPOSAL: the push cut against treading, idle variety from Epic's sample idles, weight shift, look-at. Done: a packaged film passed by a fresh reviewer. 8 h, 7%.

- `n09-9` Lean QA, first steps from the reviewed proposal: its report lines, the launch-line check on every pass, the memory line on peaks against the plan's ceiling; a test plan for phases 2 and 3, at most two pages, with the bar a build passes before it reaches him. Done: in the nightly report. 6 h, 5%.

- `n09-10` Skills from phase 1's proven methods (shopfront, slate roof, wear and dirt, night light, dressing a MetaHuman, the knit material), by helpers. Done: in .claude/skills, each proven by its next repeat. 3 h, 3%.

- `n09-11` Efficiency: the unused tools switched off (the week's measured change); same-day packaged verdicts wherever the night walk is not needed; the unexplained cache writes found; Monday's audit figures (process share, tries per fix, repeats made from a skill). Done: before and after in the overview. 5 h, 4%.

- `n09-12` Numbers from the games' files: the published inZOI mappings candidate tried; if none fits, the open-source UE4SS dumper once, licence first, never beside Unreal; Silent Hill 2 likewise; triangles, bones, detail levels and texture sizes only. Done: a budget table. 3 h, 2%.
- `n09-13` Parked cars: a cost estimate per fictional 1990 car from Fab and the image-to-3D route, licence first. Done: on his page. 2 h, 2%.

- `n09-14` The month's API credit used before it ends (about 11 November): Ron's, Sheila's and Darren's backstories and the side stories' outlines, batched at half price, after reading what is left. Done: the credit near used, the text reviewed once. 2 h, 2%.
3. Waiting, ranked (run only when the week's items wait)

1. The quay-end stop of the tester and the walkers. 2. The image-to-3D lab test (a crate, a bin, a bottle crate). 3. Mickey's front too dark at night. 4. The hill's crowns, by proper tree assets. 5. Flemish brick with burnt headers. 6. Rita's broken window. 7. The wall dish's black centre. 8. Worn paint at the front's edges. 9. Fable 5.5 against Opus when it is released.
4. Decided with this tap

The items still open from the orders of 25 October to 2 November fold into this week's item of the same aim and close there. The archive's carried items are dropped, except any that nothing in this order or its waiting list covers: those, at most ten, come back to him as one keep-or-drop list.
